visual.general_description: Guideline flow-chart of grey boxes and hollow arrows for the management of an adrenal incidentaloma, from parallel assessment to a definitive diagnosis and multidisciplinary discussion.
visual.detailed_description: Vertical flow-chart of grey rectangular boxes joined by hollow downward arrows. The top box, with white text on a dark gradient, reads "Adrenal incidentaloma"; directly beneath it is a lighter box reading "Assess in parallel". Two hollow arrows lead from it to two side-by-side boxes. The left box is titled "Potentially malignant?" and holds one bullet, "Non-contrast CT:", with nothing printed after the colon. The right box is titled "Functionally active?" and holds five bullets: "Clinical assessment", "1mg dexamethasone test", "Plasma or urinary metanephrines" with superscript 1, "Aldosterone/renin ratio" with superscript 2 and "Sex hormones and steroid precursors" with superscript 3. Hollow arrows from both boxes converge on a wide dark band reading "Aim at the establishment of a definitive diagnosis". Four hollow arrows lead down from the band. The left one leads to a box reading "Non-functioning, benign lesion (e.g. adenoma, (myelo-)lipoma)" with a darker box beneath it reading "No further investigation". The other three lead to a wide header box reading "Discuss in multidisciplinary team" above three boxes reading "Indeterminate mass", "Benign adrenal mass with MACS" and "Clinically relevant hormone excess or tumor with malignant features". No patient image, number or axis is shown.

visual.general_description: Guideline flow-chart of grey boxes and hollow arrows for assessing and managing mild autonomous cortisol secretion after a 1 mg dexamethasone suppression test.
visual.detailed_description: Vertical flow-chart of grey boxes and hollow arrows. The top box reads "Apparently benign adrenal incidentaloma"; a hollow arrow leads to a dark band reading "1 mg Dexamethasone Suppression Test (DST)". Two arrows lead from the band. The left one leads to a box "Serum cortisol ≤50 nmol/L", then to "No evidence of autonomous cortisol secretion", then by a long arrow down the left side to a box at the bottom reading "No treatment and no follow-up". The right one leads to a box "Serum cortisol ≥50 nmol/L", then a long arrow to "Overt features of Cushing syndrome?". From that box a left arrow leads to a small "Yes" box and then to a darker box reading "Overt Cushing Syndrome". A downward arrow from the question leads to "Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS)" and then to "Comorbidities potentially attributable to cortisol?" with superscript 1. Two branches leave that box. A "Yes" branch leads to "MACS confirmed? ACTH independency?" with superscript 2. From it a left arrow with a small "Yes" box leads to a darker box "Consider ACTH-dependent Cushing Syndrome" (an upward arrow into that box), and a downward "Yes" arrow leads to "Consider specific treatment" with superscript 3. A right "No" branch leads by a long arrow to "Monitor for development of comorbidities potentially attributed to cortisol" with superscript 4. No patient image or axis is shown.
